text: Salt Lake City was founded in 1847 by settlers led by Brigham Young.
Salt Lake City is part of a long line of cities along the Wasatch Front. This urban corridor is a 120-mile (190 km) stretch, with about 2.8 million people.
Four days after arriving in the Salt Lake Valley, Brigham Young marked the building site for the Salt Lake Temple. It took 40 years to finish.
Ogden is the closest sizable city to the Golden Spike site at Promontory Summit, Utah. That is where the first transcontinental railroad was joined in 1869.
Fort Utah was renamed Provo in 1850. It was named for Étienne Provost, a French-Canadian trapper who arrived in the region in 1825.
The highest temperature ever recorded in Utah was 118°F (48°C). It was recorded in south St. George.
Philo Farnsworth was an American inventor. He was granted the first patent for the television.
Philo Farnsworth was born on August 19, 1906, in a small log cabin near Beaver, Utah. He was the oldest of five children.
On September 7, 1927, Philo Farnsworth's camera tube sent its first image, a simple straight line. It went to a receiver in another room of his laboratory.
John Browning made his first gun at age 13, in his father's gun shop. He received the first of his 128 patents at age 24.
John Browning's father, Jonathan, was one of the pioneers who came to Utah. In 1852 he set up a gunsmith shop in Ogden.
Butch Cassidy was born Robert LeRoy Parker on April 13, 1866, in Beaver, Utah Territory. He was the first of thirteen children.
A Rocky Mountain elk weighs 500 to 750 lb (230 to 340 kg). Males are about 7.9 ft (2.4 m) long and females about 6.6 ft (2 m).
In the mountains, Rocky Mountain elk often stay in higher places in the warmer months. They move down lower in the winter.
Male Utah prairie dogs weigh 0.66 to 1.98 lb (0.3 to 0.9 kg) in the spring. In the summer they weigh 1.1 to 3.3 lb (0.5 to 1.5 kg).
A Utah prairie dog mother has only one litter a year, usually one to eight pups. She carries the pups for about 28 days before they are born.
A male bighorn sheep's horns can weigh up to 30 lb (14 kg). That is as much as all the bones in his body.
A desert tortoise lives 70 to 80 years on average. It grows slowly, and it has few young.
More than 16,200 bones have been dug up at the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry in Utah. Many thousands more are waiting to be dug up and studied.
Skeletons made from Cleveland-Lloyd bones are on show in more than 65 museums around the world.
Utahraptor is the largest known member of its dinosaur family. It was about 20 to 23 ft (6 to 7 m) long and weighed around 1,100 lb (500 kg).
Utahraptor had a big claw that may have been about 9.4 in (24 cm) long. Its feet seem to have had a very tight grip.
Allosaurus averaged about 25 to 26 ft (7.5 to 8 m) long. The largest ones were estimated at about 30 ft (9 m) long.
Earl Douglass and his team dug up over 700,000 lb (320,000 kg) of fossils from a single quarry at what became Dinosaur National Monument.
Bear Lake covers about 109 sq mi (280 km2). It is split about equally between Utah and Idaho. The Utah part is the second-largest natural freshwater lake in Utah, after Utah Lake.
Jedediah Smith arrived at Bear Lake in June 1827. That marked the completion of the first overland round trip to California from the United States.
The south end of Bear Lake, near Laketown, was the site of two annual Rocky Mountain Rendezvous. They were held in the summers of 1827 and 1828.
The Glen Canyon Dam that makes Lake Powell is 710 ft (216 m) high. When the lake is full, its surface is about 3,700 ft (1,100 m) above sea level.
Lake Powell took sixteen years to fill to the 3,700 ft (1,100 m) level. It got there on June 22, 1980.
Utah Lake is shallow. Its deepest spot is just under 14 ft (4.3 m), and its average depth is about 10.5 ft (3.2 m).
The most famous butte formations of Monument Valley are along the Utah–Arizona state line.
Director John Ford filmed a number of Westerns in Monument Valley. A critic wrote that its five square miles (13 km2) define the American West for moviegoers.
Goblin Valley State Park and Bryce Canyon National Park have some of the largest groups of hoodoos in the world.
Natural Bridges has three bridges. Their names are Kachina, Owachomo and Sipapu. Sipapu is the largest. All three are Hopi names.
Natural Bridges has the darkest sky ever assessed by the National Park Service Night Sky Team. It rates a Class 2 on the Bortle Dark-Sky Scale.
Rainbow Bridge has a span of 275 ft (84 m) and a height of 290 ft (88 m). It is one of the largest natural arches in the world.
Alta opened its first lift on January 15, 1939. It is one of the oldest ski resorts in the country.
Alta gets more snow than most Utah resorts. Its average annual snowfall is 543 inches (13.8 m).
Alta is one of just three ski areas in the U.S. that do not allow snowboarders.
Park City lies mostly higher than 7,000 ft (2,100 m), so it is usually cooler than Salt Lake City. Salt Lake City sits at about 4,300 ft (1,300 m).
In 2015, Park City Ski Resort and Canyons resorts merged. That created the largest ski area in the U.S.
The 2002 Winter Olympics in Salt Lake City had 2,399 athletes from 78 nations. They took part in 78 events in 15 disciplines.
